description: Negative result for i015 (SNAPSHOT=s04, BRANCH=sysfs-store-attr-terminator). Evidence: (1) fs/kernfs/file.c kernfs_fop_write_iter() (line 293) allocates kmalloc(len + 1), copies exactly len bytes via copy_from_iter, then writes buf[len] = '\0' at line 319 with comment "guarantee string termination" before dispatching to ops->write, so every standard sysfs DEVICE_ATTR/DRIVER_ATTR/BUS_ATTR/CLASS_ATTR/kobj_attribute ->store() in s04 receives a NUL-terminated buffer and the invariant cannot be violated by ordinary attribute stores. (2) The only _store-named handler in s04 that performs its own copy_from_user is drivers/edac/versal_edac.c:848 inject_data_ue_store, which is actually a debugfs .write (edac_debugfs_create_file at line 924); it clamps len = min_t(size_t, count, sizeof(buf)) on char buf[6] and explicitly writes buf[len] = '\0' (line 863) before strsep/kstrtou8, keeping the terminator in bounds - safe. (3) drivers/edac/synopsys_edac.c:1019 inject_data_error_store is a genuine DEVICE_ATTR store but performs no usercopy; it kstrtoul's the kernfs-provided buffer directly - safe. (4) The seed pattern itself is present in s04 at drivers/scsi/bfa/bfad_debugfs.c:253 and :320 (memdup_user(buf, nbytes) feeding sscanf), but those are debugfs .write handlers belonging to the debugfs-write-memdup-sscanf branch (i014), not sysfs ->store(), so they are recorded as cross-branch unresolved visibility only and were not reported under this branch. Bounded negative searches performed: all 212 memdup_user/vmemdup_user call sites enumerated (none inside a sysfs ->store()); rg -B2 -A12 over all "static ssize_t ..._store(struct" definitions found copy_from_user in only versal_edac.c; multiline rg for a device_attribute/kobj_attribute store body containing copy_from_user returned 0 matches; a 411-hit buf[count]/buf[len]/buf[size]/buf[cnt] audit surfaced only in-bounds terminator writes or unrelated code. Limitations: helper-function indirection from a ->store() to a helper doing its own copy_from_user was bounded by file-level co-occurrence spot checks rather than exhaustive line-by-line reading of all ~40 files containing both attribute types and copy_from_user; module_param .set handlers and exotic non-kernfs kobject attribute mechanisms were not individually audited; case (b) buf[count] indexing search was bounded to those four index spellings. Final artifact: agent-state/findings/i015.json with snapshots_checked ["s04"], execution_status complete, 0 findings, 4 candidates (3 safe, 1 unresolved cross-branch).
